subject: Mental Models
title: Occam's Razor
description: A short lesson to help you apply Occam's Razor.

hook.text: Your car will not start. It could be an empty tank, a dead battery, or an alien saboteur.

buildup.text: Occam's Razor says the simplest explanation that fits the evidence is most likely correct.

discovery.text: William of Ockham stated this principle around 1320.

twist.text: Simplicity does not guarantee truth. Sometimes the complex explanation is correct.

climax.text: Start with the simplest explanation and add complexity only when evidence demands it. Simplicity is the default until.

punchline.text: Start simple. Add complexity only when forced.

quiz.question: What does Occam's Razor recommend?
options: Always choose the most detailed theory
Prefer the simplest explanation that fits the evidence
